description: M12/M13 hardening: fix lexer integer overflow, add escape analysis for mutable cell leaking through closures, implement non-moving generational GC (sticky mark-bit), and add E2E concurrent stress tests.

userStories.title: Lexer rejects integer literals outside i32 range
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want the lexer to produce an error when a bare integer literal exceeds the i32 range, so I don't get silently truncated values.
acceptanceCriteria: Hex literals: if parsed value > INT32_MAX, the lexer emits a TOKEN_ERROR with message containing 'integer literal out of i32 range'
Binary literals: same range check and error
Decimal literals: same range check and error — since the lexer doesn't parse negative literals (negation is a separate op), only check val > INT32_MAX
Hex values that fit in u32 but not i32 (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFF) still error — the user must use [u32 ...]
Values that fit in i32 continue to work identically (no behavior change)
Error message includes suggestion to use [i64 ...] or [u64 ...]
Error token captures the source span (start/end position) so downstream error reporting can show the literal
Add lexer tests in test_lexer.c for: 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 2147483648, 0b followed by 33 ones, and exact boundaries (2147483647 passes, 2147483648 errors)
Test that the error message contains 'i32 range' substring
Existing lexer tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The overflow happens in src/lexer.c at lines 412 (hex), 444 (binary), and 498 (decimal) where int64_t val is cast to (int32_t) without bounds checking. The fix is to add an `if (val > INT32_MAX)` check before the cast in all three code paths, and emit TOKEN_ERROR instead. The Token struct already has payload.error_msg for error messages and start/line/col for source position.

userStories.title: Detect box/cell capture in closures passed to concurrent primitives
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the compiler to detect when a closure capturing a box or mutable cell is passed as an argument to spawn/parallel/race, and auto-pin the task to the owning worker thread.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend ast__contains_nonlocal_set_impl (or add a parallel analysis function) to also detect closures that capture variables declared with mut or box — not just direct set! usage
When a closure capturing a box/cell is passed to spawn/parallel/race, the compiler marks the generated CPS continuation as pinned (same mechanism as current set! pinning via pin_all_closures flag)
The analysis walks closure argument subtrees: if a $var reference in a closure argument resolves to a mut/box binding from an enclosing scope, that closure is flagged for pinning
Pinning behavior: pinned tasks go to the owning worker's private deque (existing infrastructure), ensuring box dereferences hit the correct thread-local state
Direct box usage in concurrent bodies (not via closure argument) continues to work via existing pinning
Update the TODO comment at compiler.c ~line 499 to document what the new analysis covers and what remains out of scope (e.g., box refs stored in collections then retrieved on another thread)
Add compiler test in test_compiler.c or test_m13.c: closure capturing a box passed to spawn — verify pinned flag is set on the continuation
Add .jacl test: closure capturing a box used inside spawn body — verify correct value is read
Existing mut_*.jacl and set_concurrent_*.jacl tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The existing pinning mechanism is in compiler.c: ast__contains_set() scans AST for set! usage and sets pin_all_closures flag. The same flag and infrastructure can be reused — the change is extending the analysis to also detect $var references to mut/box bindings, not just set! calls. CompileLocal has is_mutable field. The compiler__find_binding() function resolves variable names to their binding scope and can check is_mutable.

userStories.title: Escape analysis covers transitive capture
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the escape analysis to handle transitive capture — closure A captures a box, closure B captures A, and B is passed to spawn.
acceptanceCriteria: If a closure captures another closure that itself captures a mutable cell, and the outer closure is passed to a concurrent primitive, the task is pinned
Analysis is conservative: if unsure whether a captured variable transitively holds a mutable ref, pin (safe default)
Add compiler test: transitive capture scenario with a box — verify pinned flag is set
Add .jacl test: nested closure with box used in spawn — correct result
Existing tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: This extends US-002. The analysis from US-002 checks direct $var references to mut/box bindings. Transitive capture means: proc A captures box b, proc B captures A (via $A or calling A), B is passed to spawn. The analysis needs to track which closures capture mutable state and propagate that flag when those closures are themselves captured. Conservative approach: if any captured variable is a closure that was compiled with pin_all_closures, the capturing closure also gets pinned.

userStories.title: Add gen field to GCHeader
userStories.description: As a GC developer, I need a generation bit in the object header to distinguish young from old objects without increasing header size.
acceptanceCriteria: Reclaim bits from the mark field (currently uint8_t but only needs 1 bit): use 1 bit for mark, 1 bit for gen, leaving 6 bits unused. Or use a bitfield. The header must remain 8 bytes total.
gen is initialized to 0 (young) in gc_alloc
gc_header_of and all existing header access patterns continue to work
Document the bit layout in a comment on the GCHeader struct
All existing GC tests pass — no behavioral change yet
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: GCHeader is defined in src/gc.c around line 36. Currently: epoch(uint32_t) + mark(uint8_t) + obj_type(uint8_t) + alloc_total(uint16_t) = 8 bytes. The mark field is a full uint8_t but only uses values 0 and 1 (alternating mark bit). Simplest approach: split the mark byte into mark(1 bit) + gen(1 bit) + reserved(6 bits) using bitfields or bit masking. All mark comparisons (header->mark == current_mark) need updating to use the mask.

userStories.title: Implement promotion logic in sweep
userStories.description: As a GC developer, I need the sweep phase to promote objects that survive 2 GC cycles to the old generation.
acceptanceCriteria: An object is promoted (gen = 1) if it is live (marked or epoch-protected) after surviving 2 consecutive GC cycles

Track survival via a survive_count bit or heuristic: if an object was marked in the previous cycle AND is marked again in the current cycle, promote it. Alternatively, use a 2-bit counter carved from the reserved bits in the mark byte.
Promotion is in-place: only the gen metadata changes. No object movement, no pointer updates, no copying, no forwarding pointers
Add C-level test in test_m12.c or test_gc.c: allocate objects, run 2 GC cycles, verify promoted objects have gen == 1
Add C-level test: allocate short-lived objects, run 1 GC cycle, verify they remain gen == 0
Existing GC tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The sweep phase is in src/gc_collect.c. The gc_sweep and gc_sweep_concurrent functions iterate objects in blocks and check mark status. Promotion logic goes here: after determining an object is alive, check if it survived the previous cycle too. The mark bit alternates 0/1 each cycle, so 'survived previous cycle' can be inferred if the object's mark matches BOTH the current and previous mark values — but since marks alternate, this needs a separate tracking mechanism. Simplest: add a 2-bit survive_count in the reserved bits of the mark byte, increment on survival, promote when it reaches 2.

userStories.title: Implement per-thread remembered set
userStories.description: As a GC developer, I need a per-thread remembered set that tracks old-to-young pointers created by box/atom mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a RememberedSet structure to WorkerThread: append-only buffer of JaclVal container references, similar to GreyBuffer
Add remembered_set_init, remembered_set_push, remembered_set_drain, remembered_set_destroy functions
Extend the hybrid write barrier (gc_write_barrier or equivalent) to record a remembered set entry when an old-gen container (gen == 1) stores a young-gen value (gen == 0)
The generational check runs unconditionally (not gated on gc_active), because the remembered set must be maintained between GC cycles
Remembered set is per-thread, no contention
Drain deduplicates entries (a container mutated multiple times between GCs only appears once)
Add C-level test: mutate an old-gen atom to point to a young-gen value — verify remembered set contains the atom
Add C-level test: mutate a young-gen atom — verify remembered set is NOT populated
Existing tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The write barrier is in src/gc.c (grey_buf_push pattern). The remembered set is structurally identical to GreyBuffer (per-thread append buffer with dynamic growth). The key difference: grey buffer is only populated when gc_active is true, but the remembered set must record old->young mutations at all times. The generational check: get GCHeader of both container and new value, check gen fields. WorkerThread is defined in src/runtime.c.

userStories.title: Implement minor GC mode
userStories.description: As a GC developer, I need a minor GC mode that only traces and sweeps young-generation objects, using the remembered set for old-to-young references.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a gc_collect_minor function (or a mode flag on the existing gc_collect)
Minor GC mark phase: trace from all roots (same as full GC), but STOP tracing at old-gen objects (don't push their children onto mark stack) — except for objects in the remembered set
Minor GC also traces from remembered set entries: for each old-gen container in the set, trace its current value (which may be young)
Minor GC sweep: only sweep young objects (gen == 0). Old-gen lines/objects are untouched
After sweep, promote surviving young objects that meet the promotion threshold (US-005 logic)
Clear the remembered set after minor GC completes
Major GC (gc_collect) continues to work as before — traces everything, sweeps everything, resets all gen flags if desired
Add C-level test: allocate young and old objects, run minor GC, verify only dead young objects are reclaimed and old objects are untouched
Add C-level test: old atom pointing to young value, run minor GC, verify young value survives (reachable via remembered set)
Existing GC tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The mark phase is in src/gc_collect.c (gc_mark function). The key change for minor mode: when popping a value from the mark stack and it's a heap object with gen == 1, mark it but DON'T push its children (they're all old or will be caught by remembered set). The sweep functions (gc_sweep, gc_sweep_concurrent) need a mode flag to skip old-gen objects. Non-moving: objects stay where they are, only metadata changes.

userStories.title: GC scheduling heuristics for minor vs major
userStories.description: As a GC developer, I need the GC scheduler to choose between minor and major collection based on allocation patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: Default trigger: young allocation threshold exceeded (configurable, default ~1MB of new allocations) triggers minor GC
Major GC trigger: old generation has grown by >50% since last major GC
Emergency fallback: OOM during allocation triggers synchronous full (major) GC, same as existing 3-tier escalation
The bytes_since_gc counter on WorkerThread drives minor GC scheduling (existing infrastructure)
Add an old_gen_bytes counter that tracks total old-gen size, updated during promotion and major sweep
First GC cycle is always a major GC (no old gen exists yet)
Add C-level test: verify minor GC triggers after allocation threshold
Add C-level test: verify major GC triggers after old gen growth threshold
Existing tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: GC scheduling is currently in src/gc.c — the allocation path checks bytes_since_gc > GC_THRESHOLD and enqueues a GC task. The change: instead of always enqueuing a full GC, check whether a minor or major GC is appropriate. The gc_running atomic flag already provides mutual exclusion. Add old_gen_bytes as an atomic counter on the Runtime struct (or BlockPool). The 50% growth threshold means: if old_gen_bytes > last_major_old_gen_bytes * 1.5, trigger major.

userStories.title: E2E stress test — GC under spawn/await pressure
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a stress test that spawns many tasks producing garbage while GC runs concurrently.
acceptanceCriteria: New test/jacl/gc_stress_spawn.jacl with # mode: concurrent header
Spawns 100+ tasks, each allocating vectors/maps/strings that become garbage after use
Uses await to collect results, verifying correctness
Forces at least 2-3 GC cycles during execution (allocate enough to exceed threshold)
Correct results despite concurrent GC — verified by # expect: headers
Test runs in under 10 seconds
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: JACL proc names must be <= 7 bytes (inline string limit). Use short names like 'work', 'trash', 'batch'. The test harness auto-discovers .jacl files in test/jacl/. Use # mode: concurrent header. Each spawned task should do enough allocation to create GC pressure — e.g., build a vector of 100 elements, compute a result from it, return just the result (letting the vector become garbage).

userStories.title: E2E stress test — parallel with large persistent data structures
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a test that shares large persistent vectors/maps across parallel tasks while GC runs.
acceptanceCriteria: New test/jacl/gc_stress_persistent.jacl with # mode: concurrent header
Creates a large vector (1000+ elements) and a large map (100+ entries)
Passes these to parallel branches that read and derive new collections from them
GC runs during the parallel execution (allocation pressure from derived collections)
Verifies all branches see correct, uncorrupted data
Tests that the original collections are unchanged (persistence property)
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Building a 1000-element vector: use a recursive proc that vec-push in a loop. JACL proc names <= 7 bytes. Parallel branches should do reads (vec-get, map-get) and derivations (vec-push new elements, map-set new keys) to create allocation pressure. The key correctness check: the original vector/map values are unchanged after all parallel branches complete.

userStories.title: E2E stress test — atom contention under GC
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a test that hammers atoms with concurrent CAS operations while GC is active.
acceptanceCriteria: New test/jacl/gc_stress_atom.jacl with # mode: concurrent header
Creates an atom holding a counter value
Spawns 50+ tasks that each swap! the atom (increment counter)
GC runs during the swap operations (each task also allocates garbage to create pressure)
Final atom value is correct (all swaps applied, no lost updates)
Write barrier fires correctly — no use-after-free (test doesn't crash)
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: swap! uses CAS internally — retries on contention. The write barrier fires on successful CAS. The test verifies that the final atom value equals the sum of all increments, proving no lost updates. Each spawned task should also allocate some garbage (vectors/strings) to trigger GC during the swap operations.

userStories.title: E2E stress test — deep CPS recursion with concurrent suspension
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a test that exercises deep recursive CPS chains with interleaved spawn/await to stress continuation management under GC.
acceptanceCriteria: New test/jacl/gc_stress_deep_cps.jacl with # mode: concurrent header
Recursive proc that spawns a subtask at each level, awaits it, and recurses (at least 20 levels deep)
Each level allocates some garbage (strings, vectors) to trigger GC
Final result is correct (sum or product of recursive results)
Tests that CPS continuations are properly rooted through all GC cycles
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: This exercises the CPS recursive suspension pattern fixed in the previous PRD (ralph/cps-recursive-mutation-bugs). The test goes deeper (20 levels vs 3) and adds GC pressure at each level. The key invariant: every intermediate continuation must survive GC because it's rooted via gc_root/gc_root2 on the task.

userStories.title: E2E stress test — race with GC and write barriers
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a test that uses race with multiple branches producing garbage, verifying the winner's result survives GC.
acceptanceCriteria: New test/jacl/gc_stress_race.jacl with # mode: concurrent header
Races 5+ branches, each allocating different amounts of garbage
Winner's result is correct
Test runs multiple races in sequence to exercise GC across multiple race completions
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Race picks the first branch to complete. Losers are cooperatively cancelled. The test should run multiple sequential races (5-10) to ensure GC handles the repeated allocation/cancellation pattern. Each branch should allocate vectors/maps as garbage to create GC pressure.
